source.title: Novel High-Scalability Architecture for Photonic Deep Learning
source.authors: Yu-Xin Sun; Chun Gao; Jin Xie; Pan Wang; Ze-Jie Yu; Yi-Wei Xie; Huan Li; Dao-Xin Dai

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Figures are described in captions, but the underlying plots and supplementary sections are not included.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether residual connectivity preserves trainability in a new setting: coherent photonic networks on Omniglot, rather than the electronic image-classification settings named in V3.
record.gate_note: The paper reports photonic-network accuracy and convergence. Its spiral-task accuracy, width and power-robustness findings do not directly measure the training-error behavior named by the versions, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual connectivity and mean-field propagation principles to design photonic networks, reporting its architecture's test accuracy and optical-field dynamics. It does not measure training-error degradation with increasing depth, compare initialization-dependent learning, or otherwise test V1–V6. The abstract's qualitative claim that non-residual architectures fail to converge does not establish V3's depth-dependent training-error comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: coherent nonlinear expressivity, power stabilization, and residual connectivity enable scalable photonic networks. They attribute the Omniglot performance gain to residual connectivity preserving trainability under optical loss. Their claims should remain attributed: the supplied evidence reports test accuracy and field-propagation dynamics, without establishing depth-dependent training-error degradation or its prevention.
record.recipe_differences: Photonic coherent residual architecture evaluated on Omniglot; the text does not specify a gradient-training recipe or report training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Residual connectivity changes the reported Omniglot accuracy substantially; the paper also reports width and input-power dependence for the spiral benchmark, which is not a row for these versions.

fits_no_version.finding: On Omniglot, non-residual architectures score below 16% test accuracy, C3-enabled optical residuals reach 77.92%, and the complex-valued GELU electronic residual baseline reaches 76.88%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: C3-enabled residual connectivity substantially improves test accuracy in the tested photonic MLP-Mixer setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-field analysis and simulations describe power and correlation propagation under optical loss. Figure 4e concerns these propagation dynamics, not optimizer convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coherent nonlinearities, power compensation, and residual pathways can preserve expressive optical-field propagation in lossy photonic networks.

record.problems: The relevant comparison reports test accuracy rather than training error. Training details, uncertainty estimates, and numerical values for the convergence curves are not stated in the supplied text; supporting supplementary sections are absent.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible additional results for the claim versions were extracted. Spiral-task accuracy and power-robustness findings do not measure the training-error behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and recipe-dependent exceptions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Effects of initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons.
Training loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No claim-version verdict is warranted. The supplied text contains no numerical training-loss curves, depth-dependent training-error comparison, or initialization comparison. Figure 6 reports test accuracy; Figure 4e reports simulated power and correlation dynamics.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, and early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and teacher/student width comparisons.
Batch-normalized convolutional networks, CIFAR-10/ImageNet training error, longer training, and the cited special-initialization and no-normalization studies.
Initialization comparisons, signal/gradient propagation, and depth sweeps for plain networks.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-10, or ImageNet, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.note: The paper says all tested nonlinearities, including electronic baselines, were below 16% without residual connections. This is test accuracy, not training error.
rows.check: The below-16% value is Omniglot test accuracy. It cannot establish higher training error with increasing depth; no shallow-versus-deep comparison is reported.

rows.subject: C3-enabled optical residual network (CoP-ResNet)

rows.note: The result supports a residual-connectivity advantage in this photonic setting. Test accuracy does not establish the training-error comparison in V3.
rows.check: The 77.92% test accuracy measures the proposed photonic architecture's performance, not whether identity shortcuts prevent depth-dependent training-error degradation. The gain cannot be classified as partial evidence for V3.
